title: Far Transfer From Scaling
claimTested: Spoon reuses a scaling abstraction in a held-out software domain rather than memorizing recipe answers.

phases.purpose: Expose a scaling lesson in a non-held-out domain.

input.prompt: When scaling a recipe from 4 servings to 40, should every ingredient and every preparation step simply be multiplied by ten?

criteria: distinguishes linear quantities from bottlenecks or thresholds

phases.purpose: Test the acquired scaling structure in a held-out software domain with Teacher OFF.

input.prompt: We're moving from 100 concurrent users to 5,000. What parts of the system should I expect to scale linearly, and what parts shouldn't I blindly multiply by 50?

criteria: uses a reusable abstraction learned outside software

phases.purpose: Probe a second held-out system without naming the abstraction.

input.prompt: If I double every resource in this queue-processing system, should throughput necessarily double?

criteria: checks for a limiting component before predicting throughput
